dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kālāgninā kālapadād utthitena svakam puram | pluṣṭam vicintayed ante śāntābhāsas tadā bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one imagine one's own body (the 'city') burnt up by the fire of time (kālāgni) rising from the foot; at the end, one becomes a tranquil radiance.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: one utters a formula (aum ra-kṣa-ra-ya-uṃ tanuṃ dahayāmi namaḥ) and imagines one's body burnt by the flames of Kālāgni Rudra, rising from the toe of the right foot (kālapada); the image is of all the limitations of the body being burnt away, leaving one's essential nature, all peace. Wallis: 'one's own body (/fortress) is incinerated by the Fire of Time rising from the feet'.
dharana.technique_name: The Fire of Time Rising Through One's Own Body
dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class. For practice, use Door 024 or Door 025.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 52 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: kālapada: the toe of the right foot (commentarial)
the fire rising up through the body
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The classical map is a fire rising from the right foot through the whole body, leaving a tranquil radiance. Drawn faint: this door is studied, not drilled.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint upward flame line from one foot through a body outline, ending in a soft glow; drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Burn away (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: limitation pictured as burnt away, leaving calm light. Here it is a picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; let the body simply rest while you do
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the image: limitation burnt away, leaving tranquillity
attention.secondary: If sitting with anything, only the gentle space of Doors 024 or 025

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one imagine one's own body (the 'city') burnt up by the fire of time (kālāgni) rising from the foot; at the end, one becomes a tranquil radiance.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: while uttering a formula, one visualises the fire of time rising from the toe of the right foot and burning one's whole body, and at the end rests in a tranquil radiance. Observe-only in this school: read and understand it. For practice, use Door 024 or Door 025.

honesty.disclosure: Door 029 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 29 (verse 52) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

historical/observe_only: The classical method is a sustained visualisation of one's own body being burnt by fire, with a destruction formula. Intense imagery of one's own body burning can be distressing and is not used as a class drill. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Not led as a practice: visualising one's own body burning can be distressing. Anyone with trauma, self-harm history or strong anxiety should skip this imagery entirely. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
safety.observe_only_note: Observe-only. Imagery of one's own body burning can be distressing, especially for anyone with trauma or self-harm history; this school does not lead it. Read it as a description of letting limitation go. For practice, use a gentle space door such as Door 024 or Door 025.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 029: the fire of time rising through one's own body. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 29, verse 52. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make, and no drill. Sit comfortably while we read the verse. Its classical map is a fire rising from the foot through the body.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body rest completely. Eyes open, reading or resting softly. Attention on understanding, not on doing.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. Nothing to practise with the breath here. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the idea, not the image: what limits us can be pictured as falling away, leaving calm.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: limitation falling away, leaving calm light. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 52: describes imagining the body burnt by the fire of time rising from the foot, and a tranquil radiance at the end. Observe-only here. For practice, use Door 024 or 025.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Close the text. Take a normal breath. Look around the room and move on when ready.
